newsitem.title: CHINA: China plans music record rental to beat piracy.
newsitem.headline: China plans music record rental to beat piracy.

text.p: China will install music rental stores inside post offices nationwide to try to beat the pirate trade, the official People's Daily said on Wednesday.

As part of China's crackdown on music and software pirates, police in the boomtown of Shenzhen in southern Guangdong province carried out a dawn raid on Tuesday on an illegal laser disc factory and arrested 16 people, the Legal Daily said.
Police confiscated a production line worth HK$3.8 million (US$467,000) and 32,000 laser discs, and estimated the factory had produced 400,000 discs, the newspaper said.

The recent introduction of rewards for informers against compact disc pirates in Guangdong has paid off, officials have said, hailing the destruction of two underground video compact disc (VCD) lines in the province in recent months, it said.

In another aspect of the battle against pirates, postal authorities plan to rent and sell music from stores within certain branches across China to divert the sale of pirated products, the People's Daily said. It gave no more details.
China has come under fire from foreign companies and governments for not doing enough to combat the theft of intellectual property rights.
Last June, Beijing and Washington narrowly averted a multi-billion dollar trade war over U.S. accusations of rampant Chinese piracy of software, music and videos.
